lessons.title: TCP delivery
lessons.summary: Reliable ordered delivery within a connection.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: TCP does not preserve application message boundaries.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A receiver assumes one read contains one complete application message. Implement explicit message framing and handle partial reads.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every send corresponds to exactly one receive. This is not a sound assumption; reliable ordered delivery within a connection.

lessons.takeaway: TCP does not preserve application message boundaries.

lessons.title: UDP semantics
lessons.summary: UDP preserves datagram boundaries without built-in reliable delivery.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Applications must handle loss or duplication when their protocol requires it.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A telemetry collector sees gaps in UDP sequence numbers. Measure loss and decide whether application reliability is required.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: UDP retransmits every lost datagram automatically. This is not a sound assumption; uDP preserves datagram boundaries without built-in reliable delivery.

lessons.takeaway: Applications must handle loss or duplication when their protocol requires it.

lessons.title: DNS records
lessons.summary: An IPv4 address for a DNS name.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: AAAA records carry IPv6 addresses.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A client resolves only IPv4 while the intended endpoint is IPv6-only. Check the AAAA record and client IPv6 connectivity.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An A record contains a TCP port. This is not a sound assumption; an IPv4 address for a DNS name.

lessons.takeaway: AAAA records carry IPv6 addresses.

lessons.title: DNS caching
lessons.summary: How long a resolver may cache that record.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Lowering TTL before a change does not retroactively expire existing caches.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Some clients still reach the old address just after a DNS change. Check prior TTLs and resolver caches before declaring the update failed.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Changing a record instantly flushes every resolver cache. This is not a sound assumption; how long a resolver may cache that record.

lessons.takeaway: Lowering TTL before a change does not retroactively expire existing caches.

lessons.title: Subnets
lessons.summary: The number of network-prefix bits in the address.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Longer prefixes describe smaller address ranges.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Two hosts believed to share a subnet cannot communicate directly. Compare their addresses prefix lengths and interface configuration.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A larger prefix length always means more host addresses. This is not a sound assumption; the number of network-prefix bits in the address.

lessons.takeaway: Longer prefixes describe smaller address ranges.

lessons.title: Default routes
lessons.summary: When no more specific matching route is selected.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Longest-prefix matching favors a more specific matching route.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A host reaches its local subnet but cannot reach external networks. Inspect the selected route and default gateway reachability.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: The default route overrides every more specific route. This is not a sound assumption; when no more specific matching route is selected.

lessons.takeaway: Longest-prefix matching favors a more specific matching route.

lessons.title: ARP
lessons.summary: An IPv4 address to a link-layer address.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: ARP is scoped to the local broadcast domain.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A host cannot reach a same-subnet peer and its neighbor entry stays incomplete. Check local-link connectivity addressing and neighbor discovery evidence.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: ARP resolves domain names through recursive DNS. This is not a sound assumption; an IPv4 address to a link-layer address.

lessons.takeaway: ARP is scoped to the local broadcast domain.

lessons.title: Ports
lessons.summary: Source and destination addresses and ports.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A listening port alone does not prove application health.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A port accepts connections but requests fail immediately. Check application behavior after connection establishment.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A destination port uniquely identifies every connection globally. This is not a sound assumption; source and destination addresses and ports.

lessons.takeaway: A listening port alone does not prove application health.

lessons.title: TCP handshake
lessons.summary: Transport-level connection state between endpoints.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It does not prove that a later TLS or application exchange will succeed.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: TCP connects quickly but HTTPS fails afterward. Inspect the TLS handshake and application-layer error separately.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It proves the server certificate is trusted. This is not a sound assumption; transport-level connection state between endpoints.

lessons.takeaway: It does not prove that a later TLS or application exchange will succeed.

lessons.title: TLS identity
lessons.summary: Accepting a certificate for a different service identity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A trusted issuer alone is insufficient if the hostname does not match.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A client reports a certificate hostname mismatch. Check the requested hostname certificate names and server selection.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Any certificate from a trusted issuer matches every hostname. This is not a sound assumption; accepting a certificate for a different service identity.

lessons.takeaway: A trusted issuer alone is insufficient if the hostname does not match.

lessons.title: HTTP status
lessons.summary: The server is currently unable to handle the request.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: An HTTP response means communication reached an HTTP-speaking component.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A load balancer returns 503 while targets are marked unhealthy. Inspect target health and the reason each backend fails checks.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It proves DNS resolution failed. This is not a sound assumption; the server is currently unable to handle the request.

lessons.takeaway: An HTTP response means communication reached an HTTP-speaking component.

lessons.title: NAT state
lessons.summary: Translation devices have finite state and port resources.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Existing successful connections do not prove capacity for unlimited new ones.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: New outbound connections fail during a connection-rate spike. Inspect translation state port allocation and connection reuse.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: NAT creates infinitely many source ports. This is not a sound assumption; translation devices have finite state and port resources.

lessons.takeaway: Existing successful connections do not prove capacity for unlimited new ones.

lessons.title: Firewall direction
lessons.summary: Stateful filtering can track established flow state.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Stateless rules may require explicit rules for return traffic.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Requests leave a subnet but stateless rules reject the replies. Check return-path rules including ephemeral destination ports.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Stateless filtering always remembers connection state. This is not a sound assumption; stateful filtering can track established flow state.

lessons.takeaway: Stateless rules may require explicit rules for return traffic.

lessons.title: MTU
lessons.summary: Large packets may fail while small exchanges succeed.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Blocked path-MTU feedback can create difficult size-dependent failures.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Small requests work but larger responses stall on a tunneled path. Investigate path MTU fragmentation behavior and necessary ICMP feedback.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: MTU sets the maximum number of concurrent TCP connections. This is not a sound assumption; large packets may fail while small exchanges succeed.

lessons.takeaway: Blocked path-MTU feedback can create difficult size-dependent failures.

lessons.title: Packet loss
lessons.summary: Retransmission recovery can increase request completion time.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Loss location and timing matter more than one isolated counter.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Latency worsens during bursts and retransmissions rise. Measure loss and congestion along the actual affected path.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Any lost packet proves the destination application crashed. This is not a sound assumption; retransmission recovery can increase request completion time.

lessons.takeaway: Loss location and timing matter more than one isolated counter.

lessons.title: DNS negative caching
lessons.summary: Resolvers may cache a prior negative response.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Negative-cache lifetime can differ from the new record's TTL.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A hostname was queried before it existed and still fails at one resolver. Inspect the cached negative response and authoritative answer.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: NXDOMAIN responses can never be cached. This is not a sound assumption; resolvers may cache a prior negative response.

lessons.takeaway: Negative-cache lifetime can differ from the new record's TTL.

lessons.title: Keepalive
lessons.summary: It does not prove that the application can process a request.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Application-level health checks test behavior beyond transport state.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A connection stays established while the application worker is deadlocked. Use a meaningful application check and bounded request deadlines.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A keepalive response guarantees every database query will succeed. This is not a sound assumption; it does not prove that the application can process a request.

lessons.takeaway: Application-level health checks test behavior beyond transport state.

lessons.title: Connection pooling
lessons.summary: It reduces repeated connection setup overhead.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Pools need bounded size idle handling and timeout policy.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A service creates a new TLS connection for every short request. Measure setup cost and evaluate a bounded reusable connection pool.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A pool eliminates every network failure. This is not a sound assumption; it reduces repeated connection setup overhead.

lessons.takeaway: Pools need bounded size idle handling and timeout policy.

lessons.title: Load balancing
lessons.summary: HTTP-level fields such as host and path.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: TLS termination placement affects which component can inspect HTTP content.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Two applications share an address but require routing by URL path. Use appropriate HTTP-aware routing at a component that can inspect the request.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An L4 balancer always parses every HTTP path. This is not a sound assumption; hTTP-level fields such as host and path.

lessons.takeaway: TLS termination placement affects which component can inspect HTTP content.

lessons.title: Proxy headers
lessons.summary: Clients can forge headers unless a trusted proxy controls them.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The trusted proxy boundary must be configured explicitly.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An access rule accepts a forged forwarding header from a direct client. Restrict trusted proxies and sanitize forwarding metadata.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Any X-Forwarded-For value proves the original client identity. This is not a sound assumption; clients can forge headers unless a trusted proxy controls them.

lessons.takeaway: The trusted proxy boundary must be configured explicitly.

lessons.title: Retries
lessons.summary: They increase offered load while capacity may already be impaired.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Retry budgets backoff and jitter help control amplification.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A dependency slows and callers launch synchronized repeated requests. Bound retries and use backoff with jitter while measuring load.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every failed request should be retried immediately forever. This is not a sound assumption; they increase offered load while capacity may already be impaired.

lessons.takeaway: Retry budgets backoff and jitter help control amplification.

lessons.title: Timeout budgets
lessons.summary: Downstream work should fit within the caller's remaining budget.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A timeout does not prove the server performed no side effect.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A payment request times out and the client is about to repeat it. Check idempotency and operation status before repeating a write.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every layer should wait longer than its caller indefinitely. This is not a sound assumption; downstream work should fit within the caller's remaining budget.

lessons.takeaway: A timeout does not prove the server performed no side effect.

lessons.title: Asymmetric routing
lessons.summary: Return traffic may bypass the device holding the connection state.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Both forward and reverse paths matter when stateful devices are involved.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Packets reach the server but replies take a different firewall path and disappear. Trace both directions and inspect stateful-device routing.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Only the forward route matters for TCP connectivity. This is not a sound assumption; return traffic may bypass the device holding the connection state.

lessons.takeaway: Both forward and reverse paths matter when stateful devices are involved.

lessons.title: Anycast
lessons.summary: Multiple locations advertise reachability for the same address.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Routing chooses a path rather than an application-level session scheduler.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A route change moves traffic to another anycast location. Check route convergence and whether session state tolerates location changes.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Anycast guarantees all requests from a user reach one process forever. This is not a sound assumption; multiple locations advertise reachability for the same address.

lessons.takeaway: Routing chooses a path rather than an application-level session scheduler.

lessons.title: BGP policy
lessons.summary: Policy and path attributes guide route selection.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The selected route need not be the path with lowest measured latency.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Traffic follows an unexpected provider path despite a nearby alternative. Inspect route advertisements and policy attributes.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: BGP continuously measures application response time for every route. This is not a sound assumption; policy and path attributes guide route selection.

lessons.takeaway: The selected route need not be the path with lowest measured latency.

lessons.title: IPv6 neighbor discovery
lessons.summary: ICMPv6 Neighbor Discovery.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Blocking all ICMPv6 can break essential IPv6 operation.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: IPv6 communication breaks after a blanket ICMPv6 deny rule. Review required Neighbor Discovery and path-MTU control traffic.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: IPv6 uses IPv4 ARP broadcasts unchanged. This is not a sound assumption; iCMPv6 Neighbor Discovery.

lessons.takeaway: Blocking all ICMPv6 can break essential IPv6 operation.

lessons.title: TCP TIME_WAIT
lessons.summary: It helps handle delayed segments and the final close exchange.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Large TIME_WAIT counts need context rather than automatic deletion.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A busy client creates many short connections and accumulates TIME_WAIT sockets. Inspect connection churn port capacity and reuse patterns.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: TIME_WAIT means every socket is actively processing requests. This is not a sound assumption; it helps handle delayed segments and the final close exchange.

lessons.takeaway: Large TIME_WAIT counts need context rather than automatic deletion.

lessons.title: Queueing
lessons.summary: Packets wait longer before transmission under sustained congestion.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: More buffering can trade packet loss for queueing delay.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Throughput looks stable but interactive latency climbs during bulk transfers. Measure queueing delay and evaluate traffic management.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Increasing every buffer always lowers latency. This is not a sound assumption; packets wait longer before transmission under sustained congestion.

lessons.takeaway: More buffering can trade packet loss for queueing delay.

lessons.title: TLS termination
lessons.summary: The proxy can access plaintext application traffic.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Encryption to the backend is a separate connection policy.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A compliance requirement covers traffic between the proxy and backend. Verify and configure encryption on the backend connection too.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Terminating TLS automatically encrypts the backend hop. This is not a sound assumption; the proxy can access plaintext application traffic.

lessons.takeaway: Encryption to the backend is a separate connection policy.

lessons.title: Idempotency
lessons.summary: Repeated requests can avoid duplicating the intended effect.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Idempotency keys need scoped storage and a retention policy.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A client may retry an order after losing the response. Reuse an operation identifier and check recorded outcomes.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every HTTP POST is automatically idempotent. This is not a sound assumption; repeated requests can avoid duplicating the intended effect.

lessons.takeaway: Idempotency keys need scoped storage and a retention policy.
